question: In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler published a paper describing the formation of urea by combining which acid and ammonium in vitro?
solution:
The correct answer is __**cyanic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler synthesized **urea** for the first time by heating ammonium cyanate.
 
• The reaction involved the use of **cyanic acid** and ammonium to create ammonium cyanate, which then rearranged into urea.
 
• This discovery marked the first artificial synthesis of an organic compound from inorganic materials, **challenging the vitalism theory** that organic compounds could only be produced by living organisms.
 
• Friedrich Wöhler's experiment is considered a foundational moment in the field of organic chemistry.
 
• The reaction demonstrated that chemical processes in living organisms could be explained through physical and chemical laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urea (CO(NH₂)₂)**

 
 
• Urea is a nitrogen-containing compound that is a major end product of protein metabolism in humans and other mammals.
 
• It is widely used as a fertilizer and in industrial applications such as plastics, resins, and cosmetics.
 
 
 
• **Cyanic Acid (HOCN)**
 
 
• Cyanic acid is a simple, unstable organic acid that plays a key role in the synthesis of urea through ammonium cyanate.
 
• It is an isomer of isocyanic acid (HNCO).
 
 
 
• **Vitalism Theory**
 
 
• Vitalism was a scientific theory that posited that organic compounds could only be synthesized by living organisms due to a "vital force."
 
• Wöhler’s urea synthesis disproved this theory, demonstrating that organic compounds could be created artificially.
 
 
 
• **Friedrich Wöhler**
 
 
• Friedrich Wöhler (1800–1882) was a German chemist renowned for his pioneering contributions to organic and inorganic chemistry.
 
• His urea synthesis is celebrated as one of the most important milestones in the history of chemistry.
